newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian rupee weaker vs dollar, firms vs pound.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian rupee weaker vs dollar, firms vs pound.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee weakened against the dollar and firmed versus the pound on Friday, reflecting international trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 20.2130 for one dollar from 20.1365 on Thursday. Against the pound, the rupee traded at a mean rate of 32.180 from 32.210 on Thursday.
Dealers blamed the weaker rupee on the stronger dollar overnight on international markets.

"The dollar jumped (overnight) and this overshadowed the intervention of the central bank," one dealer said referring to a central bank dollar sale in the interbank forex market on Thursday afternoon.
The central bank intervention rate was 20.10 rupees to the dollar, close to the prevailing interbank ask (offer) rate, the dealer added.
The central bank intervention on Thursday was the second time this week.
The central bank was also seen selling dollars in the interbank forex market last Monday at the prevailing interbank ask rate in response to a shortage of forex reserves in commercial banks.
Dealers blamed the shortage situation on importers' forex demand now exceeding hard currency inflow from the island's export sectors.
